8.1 Abridged Registration for initial marketing authorisation  
 
▪ Products with marketing authorisation from one reference regulatory authority (two if API 
or fixed dose combination is new) shall be registered at NMRA within 90 days after the 
verification of the sameness of a medicinal product and taking into consideration the 
country-specific information submitted for review.  
 
▪ Chemical medicines finished products manufactured in a manufacturing site with a valid 
and relevant GMP certificate from a reference regulatory authority, and with a marketing 
authorisation in the manufacturing country and at least 3 other countries shall be registered 
at NMRA within 90 days after the verification of the sameness, bridging assessment 
depending on the scope of the GMP certificate, and taking into consideration the country-
specific information submitted for review.

pathways: (Please refer to Guideline on Registration of Medicines-GL-021)  
 
Reliance for Marketing Authorisation 
▪ Cover letter signed by the applicant’s responsible officer, including a commitment to 
inform NMRA immediately in case of withdrawal of marketing authorization in any 
country due to a quality, safety or conclusion of a benefit-risk review triggered by a safety 
issue. 
▪ Application form-Appendix 1 (including product, manufacturers, and applicant 
details); 
▪ Applicant business registration/licence information; 
▪ Contract between applicant and finished product manufacturer authorizing applicant 
to submit application and undertake related regulatory work during and after 
assessment; 
▪ Declaration of sameness of product  
▪ Declaration on regulatory status in other countries. 
▪ Product information 
▪ Proof of approval and marketing in one or more reference country, with detailed 
description of the product approved*;  
▪ Evidence of approval from the reference organization (CoPP/Public assessment 
report)  
▪ Stability study report as per Guideline on registration of medicine (GL-021,V1.0) 
covering applicable climatic zone 
▪ Lot release certificate from at least one reference NRA for vaccines/sera 
 
 
* the detailed description should include the Applicant name and unique code, 
Invented/brand name, generic name  (as it should appear in printouts), Dosage form, Strength 
(needs to be consistent with generic name), Route of administration, Description of dosage 
form, presentation and pack size (including details of different forms/items in the same 
package), Therapeutic classification, A detailed formula mentioning APIs with their quantities, 
and inactive ingredients with or without quantities, Names and addresses of API and finished 
product manufacturers, Indications, Authorized importer(s) (if applicable), Dispensing 
category, Storage conditions, Other classification (country-specific). 
 
 
** GMP certificate information should include certificate number, applicable standards,  site 
name, site address, issue date and validity, Scope: product and activities. 
 
• Clinical & non-clinical data will be verified from the full unreductant assessment report 
from reference NRA during the internal evaluation and external evaluation for biosimilars 
and NME are excluded.

Please be informed that National Medicines Regulatory Authority will accept applications for registration of foreign manufacturing sites with following GMP approvals until further notice.
PIC/s Approved (Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme)
EU GMP Approved (European Union Good Manufacturing Practices)
WHO Prequalified or WHO approved. (Inspection should be done by WHO team)
This decision will be implemented with the effect from 01/01/2025
This temporary measure is implemented to maintain a high standard of quality and safety of medicines imported to Sri Lanka and to apply reliance regulatory approach recommended by WHO.
Please note that any manufacturing site with unregistered products and without above GMP approvals will be considered case by case. The requests should be submitted to CEO, NMRA in this regard. All such requests will be subjected to manufacturing peer review committee for consideration.
This decision is only applicable for medicines manufacturing sites applications.

6. 
NMRA’S Criterion for selecting a Reference Regulatory Authority 
 
To identify its reference regulatory authorities, the NMRA will use the following 
criterion: 
• Marketing authorizations: 
o Medicines: SRA, WHO prequalification, or WLA in the scope of marketing 
authorization for medicines. 
o Vaccines: Highly performing NRAs for vaccines, WHO prequalification, or 
WLA in the scope of marketing authorization for vaccines. 
• GMP inspections: 
o Medicines and vaccines: PIC/S member, WHO prequalification, or WLA in 
the scope of GMP regulatory inspection for medicines and/or vaccines. 
In addition, the NMRA will consider the availability of the minimum required information 
for reliance in a language which can be easily understood or translated. 
 
7. 
NMRA’S process for selecting a Reference Regulatory Authority 
Considering the criterion for selecting a reference regulatory authority, the Medicine 
Regulatory Division (MRD) of NMRA can propose to the Medicine Evaluation Committee 
to consider one regulatory authority as a reference regulatory authority. In addition, based 
on the same criterion, external stakeholders may request the NMRA to consider the 
addition of another reference authority. 
On the same basis, the Medicine Evaluation Committee discuss and approves the proposed 
reference authorities. 
The current list or reference regulatory authorities is published on the NMRA website. 
(www.nmra.gov.lk)  
 
8. Reliance pathways for marketing authorizations 
 
8.1 Abridged Registration for initial marketing authorisation  
 
▪ Products with marketing authorisation from one reference regulatory authority (two if API 
or fixed dose combination is new) shall be registered at NMRA within 90 days after the 
verification of the sameness of a medicinal product and taking into consideration the 
country-specific information submitted for review.  
 
▪ Chemical medicines finished products manufactured in a manufacturing site with a valid 
and relevant GMP certificate from a reference regulatory authority, and with a marketing 
authorisation in the manufacturing country and at least 3 other countries shall be registered 
at NMRA within 90 days after the verification of the sameness, bridging assessment 
depending on the scope of the GMP certificate, and taking into consideration the country-
specific information submitted for review.
